title: Residual stress determination by the layer removal and X-ray diffraction measurement – correction method
author: Dlhý, Poduška, et al.

steps.title: Surface preparation by chemical etching
steps.instruction: Remove the machining‑induced residual stress by chemically etching the machined surface, eliminating a layer of tens to hundreds of micrometers before any X‑ray diffraction measurement.

steps.title: Verify geometric and symmetry assumptions
steps.instruction: Confirm that the cylindrical component satisfies: (1) measurement points are at least one diameter away from each free end, so the overall length is greater than twice the component diameter; (2) the residual‑stress field is axisymmetric; (3) even if measured stress is zero, X‑ray measurements must be taken over the whole cross‑section, not only near the outer surface.

steps.title: Initial XRD measurement of surface stresses
steps.instruction: Perform X‑ray diffraction on the outer surface of the cylinder and record both tangential and axial residual‑stress values.

steps.title: Remove material layer by turning
steps.instruction: Remove a concentric material layer from the cylinder by turning. Typical removed‑layer thicknesses are 1–5 mm; use finer spacing (≤1 mm) where large stress gradients are expected.

substeps.instruction: Decide the thickness of the next layer (e.g., 1 mm for the first 0–6 mm depth, 2 mm for 6–20 mm, 5 mm for 20–45 mm as an example).
Set the turning parameters and remove the chosen thickness uniformly around the cylinder.

steps.title: XRD measurement after layer removal
steps.instruction: Measure the newly exposed surface with X‑ray diffraction, again recording tangential and axial stresses at the same radial positions as before.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the measurement points span the entire cross‑section, even if the measured stress is zero.

steps.title: Repeat removal‑measurement cycles
steps.instruction: Continue the sequence of layer removal (step 4) and X‑ray measurement (step 5) until only a small fraction of the original body remains.

substeps.instruction: Document the exact thickness of each removed layer.
Maintain a list of radius positions (r) for every measurement.

steps.title: Assemble measured stress data with inner 0 MPa
steps.instruction: Create a data set that includes all measured axial and tangential stresses together with a theoretical value of 0 MPa at the inner radius (rin = 0 mm for a solid cylinder, or the actual inner radius for a hollow part).

steps.title: Set up linear stress distribution assumption
steps.instruction: Assume a linear residual‑stress variation between each pair of consecutive measured radii; this will be used for area calculations in the iterative correction.

steps.title: Run iterative evaluation correction in MATLAB
steps.instruction: Execute the MATLAB function implementing the iterative evaluation method to correct the measured stresses:

substeps.instruction: Add the 0 MPa inner‑radius value to the data set.
Calculate the unbalance U using Equation (1): U = Σ_i F_dir,i·S_dir,tot = Σ_i S_dir,i·σ_dir,i·S_dir,tot, where i indexes each radius.

For the innermost layer (rin to first measured radius), shift the stress values by the computed unbalance and recompute U repeatedly until |U| < 0.1 % of the initial unbalance for that layer set (equilibrium condition).
Treat the measured stress at the outer boundary of the current layer as fixed (boundary condition); only the inner‑radius (or previously shifted) values may be adjusted.
Add the next outer layer to the current set and repeat the shifting‑and‑U‑evaluation loop until the equilibrium condition is satisfied for the new set.
Continue adding layers outward, performing the equilibrium search each time, until all measured depths (including the outermost surface) have been incorporated.

steps.title: Obtain corrected residual stress distribution
steps.instruction: After the final iteration, extract the corrected axial and tangential residual‑stress values for every radius; these represent the original stress state of the cylinder before any material removal.
